answer: Cheap clones fail when each name must hold one physical survey stake. An applicant leases stake K-14 on the east knoll of the limestone karst, posts 36 coins for 21 days, and seats a saffron-inked serial wafer in the cap whose hash is committed before the lease starts. Every fifth morning a roving clerk photographs the wafer beside the carved stake number and files the still. Peers attest only if the knoll registry lists that serial once and the photo hash matches the commitment. A missing wafer, a reused saffron mark, or two names on one stake burns the bond and locks the site for 16 months.
